title: Khalsa' Petition Being heard in the Divine Court Question-Answer Session Between Nadar Shah And Khan Bahadur

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the supplication made by the Khalsa Singhs, Echoed in the Divine Court (of the God Almighty) A scourge (Nadar Shah) arose from Khurasan in Iran, Which fell upon Delhi (the seat of Mughal empire). (1)
lines: As the supplication made by the Khalsa Singhs,
Echoed in the Divine Court (of the God Almighty) A scourge (Nadar Shah) arose from Khurasan in Iran,
Which fell upon Delhi (the seat of Mughal empire).

blocks.text: Nadar Shah ransacked Delhi so steadily and thoroughly, That he stayed put in Delhi for full one year. After extracting thousands of crores of wealth from Delhi, He enquired from Khan Bahadur1 of Lahore about (his losses). (2)
lines: Nadar Shah ransacked Delhi so steadily and thoroughly,
That he stayed put in Delhi for full one year.
After extracting thousands of crores of wealth from Delhi,
He enquired from Khan Bahadur1 of Lahore about (his losses).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

On his return to Lahore, he asked Khan Bahadur of Lahore, About the identity of those who had robbed his war booty. He thundered that those who had waylaid his treasures, He would raze their country to dust and ashes. (3)
lines: On his return to Lahore, he asked Khan Bahadur of Lahore,
About the identity of those who had robbed his war booty.
He thundered that those who had waylaid his treasures,
He would raze their country to dust and ashes.

blocks.text: Then Khan Bahadur, responding to his query, remarked, That his plunderers did not belong to any specific country. They could feed themselves and relax while on the move, They had not any definitely fixed place for their stay. (4)
lines: Then Khan Bahadur, responding to his query, remarked,
That his plunderers did not belong to any specific country.
They could feed themselves and relax while on the move,
They had not any definitely fixed place for their stay.

blocks.text: Neither did they bother about any taste while feeding themselves, Nor did they feel any pain while being tortured. Neither did they care to drink water in the peak of summer, Nor did they need any warmth in the extreme winter. (5)
lines: Neither did they bother about any taste while feeding themselves,
Nor did they feel any pain while being tortured.
Neither did they care to drink water in the peak of summer,
Nor did they need any warmth in the extreme winter.

blocks.text: While they bothered little about their cereal food being grinded, They fought fiercely in battle with utmost agility. Each one of them could fight against a hundred adversaries, Since they were not scared of death at all. (6)
lines: While they bothered little about their cereal food being grinded,
They fought fiercely in battle with utmost agility.
Each one of them could fight against a hundred adversaries,
Since they were not scared of death at all.

blocks.text: Dohra:

They were too desperate to sacrifice their lives, For upholding their religion and its fundamental ethos. The Mughals had exhausted themselves in exterminating them, But they could not reduce their numbers in any manner. (7)
lines: They were too desperate to sacrifice their lives,
For upholding their religion and its fundamental ethos.
The Mughals had exhausted themselves in exterminating them,
But they could not reduce their numbers in any manner.

blocks.text: Then Nadar Shah enquired further from Khan Bahadur, Which prophet's descendents were these Khalsa Singhs? Did their religious order increase of its own volition, Or did they convert from some other religious order? (8)
lines: Then Nadar Shah enquired further from Khan Bahadur,
Which prophet's descendents were these Khalsa Singhs?
Did their religious order increase of its own volition,
Or did they convert from some other religious order?

blocks.text: Then Khan Bahadur traced their whole genealogy, How they owed their origin to birth of Guru Nanak? He narrated the various miracles associated with Guru Nanak, As he had heard those narrated from Janamsakhis2 . (9)
lines: Then Khan Bahadur traced their whole genealogy,
How they owed their origin to birth of Guru Nanak?
He narrated the various miracles associated with Guru Nanak,
As he had heard those narrated from Janamsakhis2 .

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He narrated how the Mughals had tortured the Nanak's followers, And the way the Mughals committed atrocities on the Singhs. He narrated the miraculous resilience that the Singhs displayed, And the way the Mughals had executed the Sikh Gurus. (10)
lines: He narrated how the Mughals had tortured the Nanak's followers,
And the way the Mughals committed atrocities on the Singhs.
He narrated the miraculous resilience that the Singhs displayed,
And the way the Mughals had executed the Sikh Gurus.

blocks.text: As Nadar Shah kept on listening to Khan Bahadur's narration, Khan Bahadur narrated all the past details of their execution. He narrated how Guru Tegh Bahadur had sacrificed his life, And the way the Guru's four Sahibzadas were murdered by Mughals. (11)
lines: As Nadar Shah kept on listening to Khan Bahadur's narration,
Khan Bahadur narrated all the past details of their execution.
He narrated how Guru Tegh Bahadur had sacrificed his life,
And the way the Guru's four Sahibzadas were murdered by Mughals.

blocks.text: Hearing this, Nadar Shah shook his head in disapproval, Remaking that the Mughals had reaped what they had sown. He further remarked how could one conquer those, Whom God Himself had come to provide protection. (12)
lines: Hearing this,
Nadar Shah shook his head in disapproval,
Remaking that the Mughals had reaped what they had sown.
He further remarked how could one conquer those,
Whom God Himself had come to provide protection.

blocks.text: Dohra:

It was in the year of seventeen hundred and ninety-six3 , That Nadar Shah had made his departure for Kandhar. After that, Khan Bahadur feeling more offended, Started persecuting the Singhs once again. (13)
lines: It was in the year of seventeen hundred and ninety-six3 ,
That Nadar Shah had made his departure for Kandhar.
After that,
Khan Bahadur feeling more offended,
Started persecuting the Singhs once again.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He himself perished while persecuting the Singhs, While some others survived to accomplish the unfinished task. I (the author) have narrated it in the same manner, As I had heard it from my ancient peers. (14)
lines: He himself perished while persecuting the Singhs,
While some others survived to accomplish the unfinished task.
I (the author) have narrated it in the same manner,
As I had heard it from my ancient peers.
